overview: A 2026-ready comprehensive roadmap for Product Designers. This path bridges the gap between raw visual design, cognitive psychology, technical feasibility, and business strategy.

steps.title: 1. Visual Perception & Design Foundations
steps.description: Mastering the 'Visual Grammar' required to create professional interfaces.
subtopics: Gestalt Principles: Proximity, Similarity, Enclosure, and Figure/Ground
Visual Hierarchy: Using scale, color, and weight to guide eye movement
Typography Systems: Line heights (1.5x rule), kerning, and accessibility-first scales
Color Theory & Systems: Semantic colors (success/error), 60-30-10 rule, and WCAG 2.1 compliance
Grid Systems: 8pt soft grid, column layouts (12-column), and modular scales
Iconography: Stroke consistency, optical balancing, and SVG optimization

steps.title: 2. Cognitive Psychology & UX Principles
steps.description: Understanding how the human brain processes information to reduce friction.
subtopics: Hick’s Law: Reducing choices to decrease decision time
Fitts's Law: Optimizing touch targets and button placement
Mental Models: Aligning UI with user expectations (Jakob's Law)
Cognitive Load: Chunking information and progressive disclosure
Emotional Design: Using the Visceral, Behavioral, and Reflective levels (Don Norman)
The Von Restorff Effect: Making critical actions stand out

steps.title: 3. User Research & Information Architecture
steps.description: Moving beyond assumptions to data-driven design decisions.
subtopics: Qualitative Research: User interviews, ethnography, and focus groups
Quantitative Research: Surveys, A/B test results, and heatmaps (Hotjar/FullStory)
Information Architecture: Sitemap nesting, taxonomy, and labeling
Card Sorting & Tree Testing: Validating navigation structures
Empathy Mapping & User Personas: Creating data-backed archetypes
Journey Mapping: Identifying pain points in the end-to-end user flow

steps.title: 4. High-Fidelity Prototyping & Logic
steps.description: Building interactive models that look and behave like real software.
subtopics: Figma Advanced: Auto-layout 5.0, Variables (Tokens), and Component Properties
Conditional Prototyping: Creating 'if/then' logic within design tools
Micro-interactions: Using 'Smart Animate' for state changes and loading states
Responsive & Adaptive Design: Breakpoints for Foldables, Desktop, and Mobile
Native OS Patterns: iOS Human Interface Guidelines vs. Android Material Design 3

steps.title: 5. Design Systems & Handoff
steps.description: Creating scalable libraries that bridge the gap between design and code.
subtopics: Atomic Design: Atoms (buttons) → Molecules (search bars) → Organisms (headers)
Design Tokens: Platform-agnostic variables for color, spacing, and motion
Documentation: Writing 'Usage Guidelines' and 'Design Specs'
Dev Handoff: Tools like Zeplin, Storybook integration, and CSS inspection
Version Control: Branching, merging, and auditing design changes in Figma

steps.title: 6. Specialized Design Domains (Choose 1-2)
steps.description: Niche skills that differentiate a senior designer from a junior.
subtopics: Saas & Dashboard Design: Managing high data density and complex tables
Mobile App Design: Gestures, haptics, and thumb-zone optimization
E-commerce UX: Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) and checkout flows
AI UX: Designing for uncertainty, LLM chat interfaces, and feedback loops
Accessibility (a11y): Screen reader testing and keyboard navigation focus states

steps.title: 7. The Business of Design
steps.description: Aligning user needs with stakeholder goals and KPIs.
subtopics: UX Metrics: Measuring success via SUS (System Usability Scale) and NPS
Product Strategy: Product-Market Fit and Value Proposition Canvas
Stakeholder Management: Presenting design 'critique' and handling pushback
Lean UX & Agile: Working in sprints and iterative 'build-measure-learn' loops

projects.name: The 'Complexity' Dashboard
projects.description: Design a B2B SaaS platform for managing logistics or cloud infra. Focus on data viz, filtering, and bulk actions.

projects.name: Social Impact / Accessibility Redesign
projects.description: Take a government or healthcare portal and redesign it for WCAG 2.1 AAA compliance.

projects.name: Future-Facing AI Assistant
projects.description: A cross-platform app where AI assists with a specific vertical (e.g., mental health or legal aid).
